objective: Deep multidisciplinary evaluation, critique, and redesign of Kalam in-person purchase assistance and companion recommendation algorithms using Behavioral Psychology, Sales/Marketing dynamics, and LLM reasoning.
audience: Product Leads, Algorithm Engineers, Torob Executives, Hackathon Judges

teams.name: Psychology Research, Analysis & Decision-Making Team
members: Dr. Cognitive Psychologist & Choice Architect (Cognitive Load, Paradox of Choice, Choice Architecture)
Behavioral Economics & Risk Perception Specialist (Prospect Theory, Loss Aversion, Mental Accounting, Anchoring)
In-Person Shopping Anxiety & Algorithmic Trust Analyst (Social friction, vendor intimidation, buyer remorse, trust calibration)

teams.name: Sales & Marketing Research, Analysis & Decision-Making Team
members: Chief Bazaar Commercial Strategist (Tehran commercial hub dynamics: Chaharsoo, Alaeddin, Hasan Abad, Lalehzar, Shoush; margin economics)
Retail Basket Optimization & Companion Economics Lead (AOV, attach rates, walk friction vs bundle discount, same-store vs cross-store)
Negotiation Dynamics & In-Store Conversion Specialist (Traditional Iranian bazaar bargaining, Ta'arof breakdown, in-store conversational leverage)

questions: Q1: How do existing algorithms (PACO, recommend.py, DCA, prompt_generator) fail or succeed from consumer psychology and behavioral economics perspectives?
Q2: How do existing algorithms align with or contradict retail store unit economics, merchant margins, and Iranian bazaar shopping realities?
Q3: What are the points of tension and synthesis between psychological reassurance (reducing choice/anxiety) and commercial basket maximization (upsell/cross-sell)?
Q4: How does the availability of high-speed LLM reasoning (e.g. Arvan AlaaS, OpenAI, Z-AI) fundamentally alter the design of real-time buyer assistance?
Q5: What is the formal specification and mathematical architecture of the newly designed BAP-LLM (Behavioral & Analytical Purchasing with LLM) algorithm?
scope: Kalam in-person shopping assistant algorithms, dynamic prompts, companion engine, basket optimization, and LLM reasoning layer
constraints: Rigorously grounded in peer-reviewed psychological and economic literature (Kahneman, Tversky, Thaler, Schwartz, Sweller, Cialdini)
Empirically faithful to Tehran offline bazaar practices and retail sales funnels
Actionable algorithmic formulas, architecture diagrams, and prompt designs
Persian cultural and conversational nuances (Ta'arof, bazaar negotiation, in-store validation)

acceptance.description: Establishment of comprehensive team charters with theoretical frameworks and analytical lenses
Exhaustive dialogue and debate transcript capturing the multidisciplinary discourse and cross-critique
Detailed comparative critique matrix of existing algorithms vs behavioral and sales benchmarks
Complete architectural and mathematical formulation of the new BAP-LLM algorithm integrating LLM intent/framing
Dynamic prompt and negotiation ammunition matrix tailored for in-store buyer enablement
